The print has «قالَ : «لاَ يَكُونُ» (zoomed, p. 1207); v1 leaves «قال» and «لا» bare. «ما» before «يبيع» is bare in the print too, so it stays.
The print has «مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِ» (zoomed, p. 1207); v1 lacks the shadda of «متفقٌ» and leaves «عليه» bare.
The print has «فَلَا يَرُدُّهُ», a damma over the shadda of the dal (zoomed, p. 1213; the same mark as «لَا يَرُدُّ» in h. 1789 below it), Muslim's wording; the text had the fatha of «يَرُدَّهُ».

The print has a kasra under the ghayn of «بِسَرْغِ» (zoomed, p. 1216), the print's single kasra for tanween, so it treats the name as declinable; the text had «بِسَرْغَ», as a diptote. Both are known readings of the place name.

The print has «فَعاثِ يَمِيناً وَعاثِ شِمالاً» with a kasra under each tha (zoomed, p. 1229): the active participle, with the print's single kasra for tanween. The text had the past verb «فَعَاثَ … وَعاثَ», also a known reading of Muslim's.
The word meanings' heading has «عاثِ» with a kasra under the tha (zoomed, p. 1232), as the matn does; the text had «عاثَ».
The word meanings quote «خَلَّةً بَيْنَ الشَّامِ» with a fatha on the ta (zoomed, p. 1232), the accusative the matn has; the text had «خَلَّةٌ».
The print has «فِي الصُّورِ» with a kasra under the fa (zoomed, p. 1234); the text left «في» bare. «لا أدري» and «يا أيها» are bare in the print too, so they stay.

The print has «إصْبَهانَ», with the hamza under the alif (zoomed, p. 1236), and its word meanings head the gloss «إصبهان»; the text had v1's «أصْبهَانَ», the city's other vocalization, which sunnah.com has.

misprint: The print ends the verb with a fatha (zoomed, p. 1237), as it does «فَيُشَبَّحَ» above; after «فَيُؤْمَرُ بِهِ فَـ» it is indicative, «فَيُؤْشَرُ», as Muslim has it.

fix: The print has «لَا يُبَايِعُهُ» with a fatha on the lam (zoomed, p. 1248); v1 leaves «لا» bare.

The print has «أَكَرَاهِيَـةَ ٱلْمَوْتِ», with a fatha on the ta marbuta shaped like the fathas on its kaf and ra, not like the damma of «رَسُولُ» beside it (zoomed, p. 1253); the text had «أكَرَاهِيَةُ». Both are good Arabic (the accusative with «أتعني» understood).

misprint: The print leaves out the ﷺ after «النَّبِيَّ» (zoomed, p. 1261: «إنَّ / النَّبِيَّ نَهَى عَمَّا»); v1 and al-Bukhari have it, so v1's text stays (rule 1, the owner's decision of 2026-11-04).

fix: The print has «سَلْ تُعْطَهْ», a sukun on the ha of pause, the same mark as on «سَلْ» and «تُشَفَّعْ» beside it and unlike the damma on its ta (zoomed, p. 1267); the text had the pronoun's damma «تُعْطَهُ».

The print has «فَلِذٰلِكَ سَعَى النَّاسُ بَيْنَهُما», with a damma on the subject of the verb (zoomed, p. 1269); the text had v1's kasra, left from its «سعْيُ النَّاسِ» after the first reading made «سعي» the verb «سَعَى».
The print has «وإنِّي» with a shadda on the nun (zoomed, p. 1276), as Muslim has; v1 leaves the nun bare in a word it marks in part.
The print has «عَلى» with a fatha on the ain (zoomed, p. 1276); v1 leaves the word bare.
The print has «فِي» with a kasra (zoomed, p. 1276); v1 leaves the word bare.
